key_insight: Latent Memory Palace (LMP) turns control policy reasoning into autoregressive latent-space variational inference, enabling adaptive, iterative compute during action selection.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to more capable continuous-control agents and a stronger action tokenizer for downstream autoregressive policies, with potential benefits in robotics and embodied AI.
method: Model reasoning as an autoregressive latent distribution over control decisions
Optimize a variational lower bound with a latent-space reinforcement learning objective
Use the same framework to learn a variable-length action tokenizer (LMP-tok)
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong empirical performance in both simulation and real-world domains, along with interpretable adaptive test-time compute and improved downstream autoregressive policies.
watch_item: Performance and interpretability gains likely depend on careful latent-space optimization and may add training/implementation complexity compared with standard control policies.
paper_title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
